newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court allows coal mine to forge ahead.
newsitem.headline: German court allows coal mine to forge ahead.

text.p: A German state court on Tuesday allowed controversial plans for Europe's largest brown coal mine to move ahead, rejecting a complaint by the environmentalist Greens party.

The Greens, who govern the state of North Rhine-Westphalia in an uneasy coalition with the Social Democrats, had filed suit seeking clarification whether the Garzweiler II mine could continue without renewed approval by the state legislature.
The Greens' opposition to the project is one of the main sticking points between them and their SPD state partners.

The state's "red-green" coalition is a focus of national attention as a microcosm of what the national government might look like if Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats were to lose the 1998 elections.

Michael Bertram, president of the North Rhine-Westphalia Constitutional Court, ruled that the Greens' complaint against the state legislature was inadmissible, and that the complaint against the state environment ministry was groundless.

The planned open-cast brown coal mine, being developed by RWE AG unit Rheinbraun AG, would be the largest in Europe. Due to begin operations in 2006, it would force 11 villages with a population of 7,500 to move.

Before the decision, state environment minister Baerbel Hoehn of the Greens party said the expected failure of the complaint was not of great significance, as it was merely the first of nine court proceedings.
